claims: The Artemis II launch is from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026, 6:24 p.m. ET.
The Artemis II launch is expected to be visible across most of Florida and parts of southern Georgia.
Visibility maps show the rocket will be visible for roughly 10–70 seconds after liftoff for, respectively, the Space Coast and further inland.
The rocket ascends to 40,000 feet before exiting direct visibility range.
10–20 seconds post-launch best viewed from Florida's Space Coast, Orlando area, Kissimmee, and north Treasure Coast.
30–40 seconds post-launch visible throughout most of Central and North Florida, including Gainesville, Ocala, and Tampa.
50–70 seconds post-launch potential visibility extends into southern Georgia, including Valdosta and near Brunswick, as well as northernmost Florida regions.
The launch is scheduled for early evening at 6:24 PM.
The launch at 6:24 PM will still be daylight.
